Anyone ever grown cherry tomatoes? I'm trying it this year. Any tips?

Watch for infections, especially if it's humid and the plants are compact. Spindly plants with small yellowish leaves and purple veins are symptoms of one infection I had, and another plant had grey fuzz growing on a leaf and died soon after.
Many varieties are indeterminate so get ready for them to grow really tall. You can snip them to keep them shorter and produce more fruit but just be ready to have the bushes get big.
How big? My regular tomatoes were seven feet last year.
They will pretty much just keep growing and growing. I start to top mine off at about 6' just to keep them manageable. They will get a lot bigger though if you let them.

I grew two types of cherry tomatoes last year - the Huskie(don't remember exactly) only got about 3.5 feet tall. The other one sprawled from one end of an 8ft box to the other, there were cherry tomatoes growing in between the big boys and romas. if you've grown regular tomatoes you shouldn't have any issues.

They take almost no effort at all. Just make sure you give your tomato plants enough space and plenty of sunlight. Keep the soil moist. I water every evening during the dry months. Watch for insects. We mix crushed egg shells and old coffee grounds into the soil.

Yes! So many!

My favorite kinds are "chocolate cherry" and "super sweet 100's"

Look up how to pick off "suckers" - they are little branches that grow in between the main stalk and a branch at a 45 degree angle. Think of holding your arm out straight, and then having a smaller arm grow out of your armpit. Get that outta here! But really, due to the angle they grow at they can't support little tomatoes so they are a waste of the plants resources, so catch them while they are little and you can scratch them off with your thumbnail ;)

When you go to transplant, you can repot them deeper then they were before and everything you bury with become more roots meaning that the roots will be stronger, resulting in a healthier plant! Take off any branches that will be buried though, because the leaves will rot underground.

I'm in mobile, so I'm not posting links to what I mean by default (cuz I'm lazy), but if you are needing clarification let me know because I can find some YouTube videos just to be clear if you want!

We found a sunny spot, prepared the soil by adding sand and some fertilizer, and then kept the soil moist through the season but otherwise it was dead simple. Other people talk about pests but other than having to put up chicken wire to keep the dogs away I had no problems.
Just give them something solid to grow up, and keep em trained and your good to go, plant does all the work.
